Your catalog is growing. Your copywriter is stretched thin. And somewhere in a spreadsheet, there are 200 products waiting for descriptions that should have gone live last month. If that sounds familiar, the problem is not your team. Writing product descriptions at scale is genuinely difficult, and the reasons go deeper than most store owners expect. 

## The hidden complexity behind a simple-looking task

A product description looks simple from the outside: a few sentences about what something does and why someone should buy it. In practice, each one involves research, judgment, and a surprising number of decisions.

Before writing a single word, someone needs to understand the product: what it does, who it is for, what makes it different from similar items, and which details matter most to a buyer. For a store with dozens of product types, that research is not a one-time task. It repeats with every new addition to the catalog.

# How do you manage product description quality across a large catalog? 

 Mar 28 

 Mar 30 

#### Topic Summary

 Summarized with AI on April 19 

Managing inconsistent product descriptions across a 400+ item Shopify catalog, with the main problem shifting from writing quality to prioritization: which pages to fix first without harming pages that already convert.

- One suggestion was to use Shopify Sidekick to review, rate, tag, and rewrite descriptions.
- The reply was that Sidekick may help with generation, but it does not clearly solve ranking/scoring weak pages by business impact.

Most actionable workflow proposed:

- Use Shopify Analytics to prioritize by revenue/traffic, following an ABC-style analysis.
- Use Google Search Console (GSC, Google’s search performance tool) to find product pages with good impressions but low click-through rate.
- Edit in small weekly batches and use a standard template for new products.

A contrasting view argued the problem is being overcomplicated:

- Do the ABC analysis in spreadsheets/processes.
- Delegate or hire copyediting help if execution is the bottleneck.
- Track changes simply, e.g. with timestamps/metafields.

Current state: no final resolution. The discussion remains open around whether automation can remove tedious scoring/ranking work enough to make long-term catalog maintenance sustainable.

# How to Build an AI Product Description Pipeline for Shopify

Manual product descriptions don't scale. Here's how I built an AI pipeline that generates accurate, SEO-optimized Shopify product copy — from data extraction through review to publish — and the prompt engineering lessons that made it work.

I run a multi-location retail business with roughly 8,000 active SKUs. For years, our product descriptions were a patchwork: manufacturer copy on some, hastily written blurbs on others, and a disturbing number that were just blank. When I finally audited our catalog, I found that over 60% of our products were running duplicate or missing descriptions. That's an SEO disaster and a customer experience failure.

Writing 5,000+ unique descriptions by hand wasn't realistic. Even at 15 minutes per product, that's over 1,200 hours of work. So I built an AI product description pipeline. Not a "paste into ChatGPT and hope for the best" workflow — a real production system with data extraction, prompt engineering, human review, and automated publishing. Here's how it works and what I learned.
